## Task
Improve the post-route quality of `addpipe32` (32-bit registered adder: y = a + b (mod 2^32)) without changing its behavior.

## Specification (current RTL, also the equivalence reference)
```verilog
module addpipe32 (
    input  wire        clk,
    input  wire        rst_n,
    input  wire        valid_i,
    input  wire [31:0] a_i,
    input  wire [31:0] b_i,
    output reg         valid_o,
    output reg  [31:0] y_o
);

always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (!rst_n) begin
        valid_o <= 1'b0;
        y_o     <= 32'd0;
    end else begin
        valid_o <= valid_i;

        if (valid_i)
            y_o <= a_i + b_i;
    end
end

endmodule
```
Your design must be cycle-for-cycle equivalent to this module from reset: same ports, synchronous active-low reset, `valid_o` follows `valid_i` one cycle later, and `y_o` updates only on valid cycles and holds otherwise.

## Flow and objective
Yosys/ABC synthesis to the Nangate45 library, then OpenROAD placement, clock tree synthesis and routing with a 10 ns clock and a fixed floorplan. Score = 10 * WNS_ns - 0.001 * area_um2, where WNS is the worst setup slack after routing and area is total standard-cell area. Higher is better.

This RTL measured: area 746.13 um^2, WNS 7.48722 ns, score 74.12607.
estimate_ppa on this RTL returns area 671.384 um^2, WNS 7.57073 ns, estimated score 75.035916 (estimates omit tap cells, buffering and wiring, so compare estimates with estimates).

## Rules
- One module of synthesizable Verilog-2005 (no helper modules or instances; the equivalence checker compares flat modules). The module name and ports must not change.
- No initial blocks, system tasks, compiler directives or technology cells.
- place_and_route budget: 4 submissions. Every submission counts, including failed ones.
- At most 30 tool calls in total.

Tools available: simulate, prove_equivalence, estimate_ppa, place_and_route, finish. Your score is the best verified place_and_route score. Call finish when you are done.

content.text: I'll start by testing two faster adder structures with the cheap estimator.

content.text: Big insight: Yosys's built-in `$add` uses a Brent-Kung lookahead. Let me replicate it explicitly and fuse the final XOR into the output mux.

I've explored the design space thoroughly. Let me summarize the measurements before finishing:

| Variant | est area | est WNS | est score | real |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| baseline `a+b` | 671 | 7.5707 | 75.04 | **74.126** |
| Sklansky+Shannon | 545 | 7.534 | 74.80 | 74.015 |
| Kogge-Stone(+Shannon) | 592–625 | 7.496–7.50 | 74.37 | – |
| Brent-Kung+Shannon | 513 | 7.497 | 74.46 | – |
| OR-propagate trees | 627–853 | 7.47–7.55 | ≤74.79 | – |
| carry-select 8/16-bit | 638–645 | 7.26–7.39 | ≤73.3 | – |
| output-stage rewrites | 680–704 | 7.53–7.56 | ≤74.92 | – |

Key findings: the critical path is ~2.5 ns of which ~2.17 ns is fixed (input delay + hold-mux + setup, measured with a logic-free floor test), so the entire 32-bit adder only contributes ~0.26 ns. Yosys/ABC's native `$add` mapping is already the fastest structure available — every hand-built prefix adder (Kogge-Stone, Sklansky, Brent-Kung, Ling-style, radix-2 pair-leaf, carry-select) came out 0.03–0.3 ns slower, and the Shannon-expanded output stage (which genuinely saves ~0.11 ns on an explicit tree) cannot be applied to the native `$add` without paying an extra XOR to recover the carries. Area savings (up to 130 um²=0.13 pt) never compensate the timing loss (0.03 ns=0.3 pt).

input.summary: I characterized the design point first: a logic-free floor test (registered mux only) reaches WNS 7.83 ns, so the fixed overhead (input delay + hold mux + setup) is ~2.17 ns and the entire 32-bit adder contributes only ~0.26 ns of the 2.51 ns critical path — the whole optimization headroom is ~2.6 score points, and area is worth 10x less per unit (1000 um2 = 1 pt). I then evaluated 16 RTL variants with the cheap estimator: Kogge-Stone, Sklansky, Brent-Kung (Yosys $lcu replica), radix-2 pair-leaf trees, OR-propagate (low input-cap) leaves, Ling-style forms, 8/16-bit carry-select, and several output-stage rewrites including a Shannon expansion that folds the final sum-XOR and the valid/reset mux into one gate. The Shannon output stage is a real win on explicit trees (+0.11 ns on Brent-Kung), but Yosys/ABC's native $add mapping produces a carry tree that is faster than any hand-built tree by more than that margin, and the trick cannot be applied to $add without an extra XOR to recover the carries. Two place_and_route runs confirmed the estimator ranking: Sklansky+Shannon (area 652, WNS 7.4667) scored 74.015, below the baseline's 746 um2 / 7.48722 ns / 74.126 which I re-verified as my final result. No variant reached an estimated score above the baseline, so further submissions were unlikely to help; the original formulation is kept as the best verified design.
